title: Claim (temporal fact)
description: v2. Immutable, bitemporal, append-only. A claim is never edited: changes and corrections append new records with supersession links (TEMPORAL.md). The v1.0 history[] array is retired — history IS the record set.

predicate.description: From data/schema/predicates.yaml, which also declares each predicate's temporal_kind.

value.description: Structured where possible. The literal 'unknown' is a legal, publishable value.

conditions.description: Mandatory for measurement and series kinds.

scope.description: WHO this claim is true for. Added 2026-08-04 after the Atlas computed a confident cost figure from an operator-specific input without telling the reader. 'Measured' was never sufficient — measured FOR WHOM is the question that determines whether a fact transfers. universal: holds regardless (arithmetic, definitions). vendor: holds for this product (most Class A spec facts). harness: determined by tooling, not by the person. operator: varies by individual. workload: varies by the kind of work being done.

elicit.description: REQUIRED when scope is harness, operator, or workload AND the claim feeds a computation. The scope field generates this: if a fact does not transfer, the engine must ask rather than assume. This is the claim carrying the question needed to make it applicable to a given reader.

question.description: One question, in the reader's language, not the system's. Asked only when the answer is actually sensitive to it (DECISION.md §8 — value of information, pointed at the reader).

default.description: LOCKED to null. A default here would silently reintroduce exactly the failure this field exists to prevent — an unasked assumption presented as a computed answer.

supersession_reason.description: Required for correction and retraction. This is what the corrections register publishes.

then.description: SCOPE-1: a non-transferable claim must carry the question that makes it transferable, or the engine has no honest way to apply it to a reader.
Measurements and series are never carried forward and never render without conditions (TEMPORAL.md §2, §7.1).
Corrections must say what was wrong. CONSTITUTION §11.
Release dates and acquisitions do not decay (TEMPORAL.md §6).
